newsitem.title: USA: Schawk agrees to merger settlement.
newsitem.headline: Schawk agrees to merger settlement.

text.p: Schawk Inc said Friday it will pay up to $80,000 as part of a settlement on all claims arising out of two class-action lawsuits brought against it in relation to its merger with Filtertek Inc.

The settlement involves the $80,000 payment for expenses and the transfer by two of Schawk's principal stockholders and directors -- Clarence Schawk and David Schawk -- of 159,521 shares of its Class A common stock to Schawk stockholders.

The transfer will be made to shareholders of record as of December 31, 1994, the date of the merger. The Schawk family, their relatives and directors or officers of Schawk will not be eligible to share in the transfer.
In addition, a "put" was granted to stockholders permitting them to require Schawk to buy back their stock at certain scheduled prices.
The settlement is subject to approval by the U.S. District Court in the Northern District of Illinois. A court hearing is scheduled for May 15.
David Schawk said in a statement that the settlement was not evidence of any wrongdoing. He said he was issuing the statement on behalf of himself and his father, Clarence.

"My father and I still strongly believe that the merger of Schawk Inc into Filtertek Inc was in the best interests of and entirely fair to the Filtertek stockholders," he said. "The rise in Schawk's stock price since we announced the sale of Schawk's plastics group (the older Filtertek Inc) confirms this judgment."
"We simply wanted to spare the company the time and expense of a lengthy trial," David Schawk added.
